title: Take Away, Count Up
topic: Subtraction within 100: take away and count up

items.hint: Take away 2 tens. The ones stay the same.
steps: Take away 2 tens: 3 tens and 8 ones.

slips.say: 56 is what you get if you take away 2 ones. Take away 2 tens (20) instead.
78 is 58 + 20. We take away.

tpl.hint: Take away {t} tens. The ones stay the same.
steps: {a} is made of tens and ones.

items.hint: Take away 3 ones. The tens stay the same.
steps: Take away 3 ones: 7 tens and 3 ones.

slips.say: 79 is 76 + 3. We take away.
46 is what you get if you take away 3 tens. Take away 3 ones instead.

tpl.hint: Take away {o} ones. The tens stay the same.
steps: {a} is made of tens and ones.
Take away {o} ones. The tens do not change.

items.hint: 25 is 2 tens and 5 ones. Take away 2 tens first, then 5 ones.

slips.say: 93 is 68 + 25. We take away.
53 is 68 - 15. Take away 2 tens, not 1.

tpl.hint: {b} is {tb} tens and {ob} ones. Take away the tens first, then the ones.

items.q: A bus has 86 seats. Children sit on 32 of them. How many seats are empty?
items.hint: Empty seats are what is left when we take away the seats that have a child.

slips.say: 118 is 86 + 32. Empty means we take away.

tpl.q: A bus has {a} seats. Children sit on {b} of them. How many seats are empty?
tpl.hint: Empty seats are what is left when we take away the seats that have a child.
steps: Take away the tens of {b} from {a}.

items.hint: To check a take away, add the answer back to the number you took away. Do you get the start?
steps: The answer is 33. The number taken away is 24.
57 is the number we started with, so the take away is right.

slips.say: 57 + 24 starts from the big number. Add the answer 33 to the 24 instead.

items.q: Ben has 38 stickers. Mei has 62 stickers. How many more stickers does Mei have than Ben?
items.hint: Count up from 38: hop to the next ten, jump by tens, hop to 62.

slips.say: 100 is 38 + 62. We want the gap between them.
36 does not count the 2 tens jump. 40 to 60 is 20.

tpl.q: Ben has {x} stickers. Mei has {y} stickers. How many more stickers does Mei have than Ben?
tpl.hint: Count up from {x}: hop to the next ten, jump by tens, hop to {y}.
steps: Start at {x}. Count up to the next ten.
Jump by tens, then hop to {y}.
Add the hops and jumps: the gap is {ans}.

items.hint: What is the next ten after 58? How far is it? Then how far to 62?

slips.say: 120 is 62 + 58. We want the gap.
14 is 62 - 48. Count up from 58 to 62.

tpl.hint: What is the next ten after {b}? How far is it? Then how far to {a}?
steps: Hop from {b} to the next ten.

items.q: Ali has 24 stickers and Ben has 31 stickers. Then each child gets 10 more stickers. How many more stickers than Ali does Ben have now?
items.hint: Find each child's new number. Or think: both got the same 10 more.
steps: Ali now has 34. Ben now has 41.
The gap was 7 before, because both got the same amount.

slips.say: 17 is 7 + 10. Both children get 10, so the gap does not change.
41 is Ben's number now. We want how many MORE than Ali.

tpl.q: Ali has {a} stickers and Ben has {b} stickers. Then each child gets {c} more stickers. How many more stickers than Ali does Ben have now?
tpl.hint: Find each child's new number. Or think: both got the same {c} more.
steps: Find the gap between the two new numbers.

items.q: To find 82 - 79, which way is quickest?
options: Take away 7 tens, then take away 9 ones
items.hint: Look at the two numbers. Are they close together or far apart?
steps: Counting up gives 3 in two short steps, so it is quickest.

slips.say: Adding gives a greater number. We want the gap between them.

items.q: A crate has 100 eggs. Ali sells 64 of them. How many eggs are left?
items.hint: Count up from 64: hop to the next ten, then jump by tens to 100.

slips.say: 164 is 100 + 64. Ali sold some eggs, so take away.
46 is 100 - 54. Count up from 64.

tpl.q: A crate has 100 eggs. Ali sells {n} of them. How many eggs are left?
tpl.hint: Count up from {n}: hop to the next ten, then jump by tens to 100.
steps: Hop from {n} to the next ten.
Add the hop and the jumps: {ans} eggs are left.

items.q: 83 - 47 = 86 - ___. What number goes in the blank?
items.hint: 83 went up by 3 to make 86. What must 47 do so the gap stays the same?
steps: The top number went up by 3: 83 to 86.
The bottom number must go up by 3 too: 47 to 50.

slips.say: 47 is the old bottom number. The top number went up by 3, so the bottom number goes up by 3 too.
44 is 47 - 3. Add the same number to both.

tpl.q: {a} - {b} = {a2} - ___. What number goes in the blank?
tpl.hint: {a} went up by {c} to make {a2}. What must {b} do so the gap stays the same?
steps: The top number went up by {c}.
The bottom number must go up by {c} too.

items.q: Ali has fewer stickers than Mei. The gap is 24. Mei has 71 stickers. How many stickers does Ali have?
items.hint: Ali is 24 below Mei. Take away the gap from Mei's number.

slips.say: 95 is 71 + 24. Ali has fewer, so take away.
24 is the gap. Ali has 24 fewer than Mei, so take 24 away from Mei's number.

tpl.q: Ali has fewer stickers than Mei. The gap is {g}. Mei has {m} stickers. How many stickers does Ali have?
tpl.hint: Ali is {g} below Mei. Take away the gap from Mei's number.

items.q: Make up a story about the gap between two numbers, like two piles or two towers. Find the gap by counting up. Then check by adding.
items.hint: Pick two numbers first, one greater than the other. Then write the story.
steps: Write the two numbers in your story and ask how many more.
Count up from the smaller number: hop to the next ten, jump by tens, hop to the greater number.

Check: the smaller number plus your gap should make the greater number. For example: Ali has 47 cards and Ben has 71 cards. 47 to 50 is 3, 50 to 70 is 20, 70 to 71 is 1, so the gap is 24. Check: 47 + 24 = 71.
